audio.transcript: Working from home sounded ideal before I tried it. I imagined I would have more time and fewer interruptions. In practice, I missed the quick conversations that helped me solve problems, and I found it difficult to stop working at the end of the day. After a few months I changed my routine: I worked at home only on tasks that required quiet concentration and went to the office for collaborative work. I now think remote work can be excellent, but whether it works depends strongly on the person's role, home environment and personality.

audio.transcript: Good sleep is not only about the number of hours in bed. The conditions around us matter as well. For many people, blocking unwanted light and reducing noise make a noticeable difference. However, tiredness is not always easy to recognise. People may become impatient or make small mistakes without realising that poor sleep is the cause. Public discussion sometimes treats sleep as a simple lifestyle trend, but it is better understood as a basic part of health that affects judgement, mood and performance.
